hints: Focus on what that yellow precipitate tells you, it is the classic tri-iodomethane test for a very specific alcohol group.
Recall that only an alcohol containing the group $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ gives a positive result, so look for a carbon with both an $\text{OH}$ and a $\text{CH}_3$ attached.
Check each ring structure carefully to see where the $\text{OH}$ sits, only one has the $\text{OH}$ carbon directly joined to a methyl group with a hydrogen still on it.
walkthrough:
**Recognise the test**

Great spot, yellow precipitate with alkaline $\text{I}_2(aq)$ means a positive iodoform test. For an alcohol, this is only given by one special arrangement.

Test result:
$$\text{yellow solid} = \text{CHI}_3 \text{ (tri-iodomethane, iodoform)}$$

**Recall the group needed**

Think simply: the molecule must contain an ethan-1-ol fragment. That is a carbon bearing $\text{OH}$ and $\text{H}$, joined directly to a $\text{CH}_3$ group.

Required group:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)R}$$

**Apply to the four structures**

Now look at the $\text{C-OH}$ carbon in each option. Options A and B have $\text{-CH(OH)-}$ or $\text{-CH}_2\text{OH}$ on a ring but no $\text{CH}_3$ on that same carbon. Option C is tertiary with no H on the $\text{C-OH}$.

Only one structure shows $\text{CH}_3\text{-CH(OH)-}$ attached to the cyclohexane ring, and that is the alcohol that can be oxidised to give $\text{CHI}_3$.

options.A: Incorrect. This is 2,4-dimethylcyclohexan-1-ol, a secondary alcohol but the $\text{C-OH}$ is part of the ring and is not directly bonded to a $\text{CH}_3$ group. It lacks the $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ unit, so no iodoform forms.
options.B: Incorrect. This has a $\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ side chain, a primary alcohol of type $\text{RCH}_2\text{OH}$. The $\text{OH}$ carbon is not joined to a methyl group in the $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ arrangement, so the test is negative.
options.C: Incorrect. This is a tertiary alcohol, $\text{(CH}_3\text{)C(OH)(ring)}$. There is no hydrogen on the $\text{C-OH}$ carbon, so it cannot be oxidised by the alkaline iodine and cannot give the $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ intermediate needed for $\text{CHI}_3$.
options.D: Correct. This is 1-cyclohexylethan-1-ol, $\text{C}_6\text{H}_{11}\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$. It clearly contains the $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ group, which is oxidised then cleaved by alkaline $\text{I}_2(aq)$ to give the yellow precipitate of $\text{CHI}_3$.
